pull off the following stunt in a game, I need to know if it was even
worth worrying about.

(negating Burst of Sunlight) and use Fast Hands to steal the Ivory Bow

prevent the use of the weapon to threaten ag-damage?

> prevent the use of the weapon to threaten ag-damage?

The superior Fast Hands will prevent the use of the weapon, but
it doesn't prevent the attempt to use the weapon. The attempt
comes when the minion announces that he will strike with the
weapon. So Rotschreck can still be played on Donal if the
thaumaturgist chooses "Ivory Bow" as his strike.

I'm pretty sure the sequence of combat is close to the following:

1. Determine Range. Use maneuvers to set the range to close or long.
2. Strike. Announce and resolve strikes. (Repeat for additional strikes)
2.1 Announce First Strike
2.2 Announce Strike (non First Strike)
2.3 Resolve First Strike
2.4 Resolve Strike (non First Strike)
3. Press. Use presses to continue into another round or to end combat.

Since the Resolve First Strike phase takes place after the Announce Strike
phase, the opposing minion did get to attempt the damage, he just didn't
get the damage (from the non First Strike) resolved.

Thinking about this though, I have a question or three for the older
players. Did Resolve First Strike used to be before Announce Strike? Did
First Strike used to beat out Dodge or S:CE? Does anyone think that First
Strike should beat out Dodge and S:CE?

p.

What it'll do to game play is in there as well, but to recap:

If FS beats dodge, but not S:CE, it fixes nothing, as dodge isn't really a
problem for combat decks--between presses and additional strikes, both of which
are highly available to all clans who have access to FS (who--the Assamites and
Celerity clans?), dodges have little effect on any clans who have access to FS.

If FS beats S:CE also, it becomes slightly helpful for the Assamites, but no
one else (as the Brujah have access to IG, making the FS plan uneccessary and
inferior in any circumstance), but probably not enough to warrant changing the
rules--as it is, the Assamites have access to Psyche, which will be pretty much
just as efective as FS (if it beat S:CE).

As I've mentioned earlier. S:CE doesn't always represent the ability to
avoid or evade attacks, it sometimes represents the ability to prevent the
attack altogether (or in meaning, that the attack could NEVER have
happened). In the case of Majesty, it means that the vampire has such an
awesome presence that they could not have been attacked in the first place.
The same goes for Staredown in which the vampire's ability to intimidate his
opponent causes the opponent to run in fear (at Superior, at inferior it's
only powerful enough to prevent one attack). Earth Meld for instance is the
ability of a vampire to hide in the ground and Form of Mist similarly turns
the vampire into a mostly invulnerable form. Why should First Strike in
these cases change anything? Does a surprise attack really mean anything to
a vampire that is alread in the ground or who has a strong enough Presence
that he couldn't attack? Does the speed of their attack effect this either?
No.
Ok, so the argument comes down to a game mechanic. As mentioned, some
clans are helpless to S:CE and others aren't. I personally don't have a fix
for the problem because all of the possibilities I've found cause just as
many problems as the current rules. The only thing I think we can hope for
is that some of the few cards that are released in this mini-mini set later
this year will get around S:CE.

Vince

While in the case of a First Strike steal/destroy weapon
(or strike: combat ends), the weapon is not used (so
would not self-burn in the case of a grenade), the
attempt to use the weapon is still there - the attempt
is identified in the "choose strike" phase.

Rotschreck could be played on an Ivory Bow strike even
if the opposing vamp attempts to steal/destroy the Bow
with First Strike (or attempts to strike: combat ends).

The wording may be sketchy, but the difference is that you did get to try
to play the card before the strike is taken away (unlike HL where you
didn't even get to try).

> >>You're stuck with nothing, rather than being able to choose a

>

I agree that you can't strike with a weapon that you don't have. But the
ruling that you don't get a different strike leads me to think that you
did actually get the attempt to use the weapon. Therefore the Rotschreck
can be played.

For instance, if you don't intend to use the weapon, and try to strike
with something else, your attempt is successful and weapon gets stolen by
the opposing minion. If you choose the weapon and it gets stolen, your
attempt is not successful. It's not really like Hidden Lurker where you
never had a strike attempt of any kind to begin with.

I look at it as though, if the weapon were a gun, he takes it as you are
firing, but you hit nothing. Same effect. You are stuck with that
strike, but there isn't an effect.

> To be honest, I would prefer to force the minion whose weapon was being
> stolen to choose a different strike. It would clear up the timing issue
> altogether.

I would prefer it that way as well I think. But then I'd prefer it if FS
actually resolved before normal strikes were stated. That's just me
though.
